source: lane T-editor round 3, fresh J19 copy (v0.1.4), core r14 note, event 603

event.text:
- NEW MOVE: rush (F, shield charge). Move id `rush`, clip `body_check`, wind 18 / active 28 / recovery 40. While active it runs straight along its facing at 3 × walk speed (10.8 m/s, about 5 m). It hits anyone in front of it (reach 1.9 m, arc 110°), each person once. Each one hit takes 8 damage and is floored: contact type `knockdown`, move `rush`, 70 frames down plus a 50-frame slow getup, thrown 2.4 m. A rival facing it with the shield up stops it dead. That contact is type `blocked_heavy` and gives the loud clang. The blocker takes stamina damage of 30 × his block factor and 20 frames of BLOCKSTUN. The charger is thrown back 1.3 m and is GUARDBROKEN for 70 frames, so his shield is flung wide. Stamina cost 25, cooldown 240 frames.
- NEW MOVE: slam (C, leaping slam). Move id `slam`, clip `strike_heavy`, wind 36 / active 4 / recovery 46. During the wind-up he crouches for 8 frames, then leaps 1.3 m up and 2.4 m forward. The leap height is drawn only: it is an offset on the figure, and the body stays on the ground. A red ring marks the landing spot. On landing, a dust shockwave ring spreads, a ring of dust bursts goes up, the camera kicks (0.3), and stone and break sounds play. Everyone within 2.8 m is floored whether their shield is up or not: contact `knockdown`, move `slam`, 12 damage, a 12-frame freeze on slammer and victim, 60 frames down plus a 45-frame getup, thrown 1.8 m. A roll or dodge in i-frames counts as `evaded`. Stamina cost 25, cooldown 300 frames. The slammer gets no freeze of his own when the slam lands on nobody.
- Input: two new actions, `rush` (F) and `slam` (C). The fighter's `pad` gains the keys `rush` and `slam`. Brains that leave them out still work, because the pad is read with a default.
- Fighter: new `cd` dictionary and `ready(m)` method. The 8-frame buffer takes the new moves only when they are off cooldown.
- Contact: the big moves get their own function, `_big` in contact.gd. Like other contacts they pass through `gate_contact` and `record`. A knockdown carries `cause` `rush` or `slam`, and new lines under `why` in tuning.json explain each to the player.
- Rival AI (brain.gd): once a rival's reaction time has passed, it does the following. It raises its shield against a charge coming straight at it. Whether it braces is decided once per charge, with the tier's defend chance. It runs out of a slam's ring. When its line to the locked target is open and the target's shield is down (2.6 to 6 m away), it charges with a chance of 0.025 a frame. It slams when the landing ring holds at least 2 rivals, or every rival still standing if fewer, with a chance of 0.03 a frame. None of this happens during the lesson. These figures are in `tuning.json` under `big`.
- bot_player.gd now always plays 6000 frames instead of stopping once its checks pass. After 3 blocks, outside the lesson, it uses slam and rush wherever they can land. It reports `metrics.moves` with `started`, `landed` and `last_f` for `rush` and `slam`, counted from the game's contact events. The ok rule (3+ blocks, 1+ bash, 30+ damage) is unchanged.
- The teammates' brains belong to another package, so Oda and Finn don't choose these moves by themselves yet. The moves do work for them through the same pad. The rally mod gives horn charge on `blocked_heavy`, so stopping a charge with your shield also charges your horn.
- NOT DONE: the player asked that every fighter, the mates included, use the shield charge and the slam. That needs the crew brain under scripts/crew or gen/mod_crew.gd, which is outside my scope. The exact edit: in the mates' think, set `f.pad["rush"]` or `f.pad["slam"]` to true when `f.ready("rush")` or `f.ready("slam")` is true and an open line or a crowd is in front, and set `f.pad["guard"]` against a rival whose `move == "rush"` while that rival is in WINDUP or ACTIVE.
